scope: static source review of AOSP android16-release plus the pinned LineageOS framework commit; paired with read-only runtime checks on the installed phone

findings.biometric_aidl_hal_tree: contains common, face and fingerprint; no iris AIDL HAL
findings.auth_service: still reads legacy TYPE_IRIS sensor configuration and calls IIrisService.registerAuthenticators with sensor properties
findings.aosp_android16_framework_cross_check: AOSP android16-release retains the legacy iris registration hook in AuthService, but its biometric HAL tree contains no iris HAL and BiometricService has no TYPE_IRIS-specific branch. BiometricService does expose generic IBiometricAuthenticator registration and sensor/session handling. Lineage's IrisService is therefore a compatibility adapter into that generic service path, not a platform iris AIDL HAL.
findings.lineage_iris_service: IrisService is present. Pinned SystemServer starts it only when FEATURE_IRIS is declared. AuthService parses TYPE_IRIS config and forwards sensor properties through IIrisService; IrisService registers a generic IBiometricAuthenticator with modality TYPE_IRIS.
findings.lineage_iris_authenticator: stub at the pinned commit: it stores the IIrisService reference but does not use it; hardware/enrollment return false, sensor properties and test/proto data return null, auth prepare/start/cancel and invalidation are empty, authenticator ID is always 0, and lockout always reports none.
findings.runtime_phone: service check iris reports not found; pm list features has no iris/face/biometric feature match; dumpsys biometric has no registered sensors
findings.implication: The bring-up needs the legacy IrisService feature/config wiring plus a camera-backed IBiometricAuthenticator and lifecycle. Class 1 cannot authorize apps or keystore keys and does not require a Strong-class HAT. The installed AuthSession accepts a non-Strong success without a token, but this is the BiometricPrompt dialog path; it is not by itself a Keyguard unlock callback. The camera-backed software matcher must not fabricate a token.
findings.class1_lock_screen_route: Android 16 defines Class 1 (Convenience) for lockscreen-only biometric use; the CDD does not permit app-facing biometric APIs or keystore-key authorization for Class 1. The pinned BiometricService accepts BIOMETRIC_CONVENIENCE registration. A non-Strong AuthSession result can be delivered without a HAT in the BiometricPrompt dialog flow, but this does not establish the separate Keyguard modality callback. The device still does not qualify: FAR/SAR and presentation-attack metrics are unmeasured, and enrollment/removal lifecycle and trustworthy persistent template storage are absent.
class1_cdd_gates: FAR below 0.002%; Android protocol spoof/imposter acceptance no higher than 30% for Level A and 40% for Level B PAI species (40% maximum per species)
credential-confirmed enrollment using a device credential secured by TEE; delete identifiable iris data when user or primary credential is removed
honor DevicePolicyManager.KEYGUARD_DISABLE_IRIS and rate-limit attempts; no more than 20 false trials before credential fallback, with at least 90 seconds backoff
fallback to primary credential at least every 24 hours and after 4 hours idle or 3 failed biometric attempts; disable biometrics once primary-authentication backoff triggers
no third-party biometric API or keystore-key authorization for Class 1
findings.exact_keyguard_route: The installed framework.jar defines BiometricSourceType.IRIS (ordinal 2), but IrisManager has only an empty constructor. IIrisService only registers authenticators; it cannot authenticate or enroll. Installed SystemUI has no IrisManager or TYPE_IRIS Keyguard path: its KeyguardUpdateMonitor switch maps only FINGERPRINT and FACE and rejects IRIS in isUnlockingWithBiometricAllowed. Generic biometric callbacks exist, but no iris-specific listener/request route is wired. The installed IBiometricService exposes generic authenticate(PromptInfo) and cancelAuthentication operations but no authenticateForKeyguard operation. BiometricService source explicitly allows BIOMETRIC_CONVENIENCE registration without making the sensor available to android.hardware.biometrics APIs, so an ordinary BiometricPrompt call is not a supported Class 1 bridge. A dedicated system-internal Keyguard request/cancel/result path plus the sensor authenticator is needed. IrisService already registers a generic authenticator with BiometricService, but this registration is not the direct Keyguard modality path. The pinned FaceService has a separate modality authenticate() call that schedules through a sensor provider and a separate prepareForAuthentication() path for BiometricPrompt. Mirror that split for iris and explicitly gate the direct request to Keyguard/SystemUI. The existing BiometricPrompt AuthSession is not that Keyguard route. Installed AuthSession.onAuthenticationSucceeded accepts an empty token for non-Strong success, drops any non-Strong token, and still calls StatusBarService.onBiometricAuthenticated(modality). This confirms the BiometricPrompt success notification path only; it does not prove a Keyguard unlock callback. The pinned Lineage KeyguardUpdateMonitor subscribes to FaceAuthenticationListener events and routes success, failure, acquired, error, lockout and enrollment changes into Keyguard state. The installed DEX also contains FaceManager references. The iris design must add a system-only request/cancel/result route and integrate it with Keyguard state handling.
findings.class1_prompt_filter: AOSP BiometricManager documents BIOMETRIC_CONVENIENCE (0x0FFF) as intended for DeviceConfig strength adjustment and explicitly invalid for public android.hardware.biometrics APIs. BiometricService.Utils.getPublicBiometricStrength() masks requested strengths with BIOMETRIC_WEAK, so Class 1 does not become an eligible sensor in the normal PromptInfo/PreAuthInfo flow. Android permits Class 1 for lockscreen use, so this confirms the required integration is a separate privileged Keyguard path, not ordinary BiometricPrompt.
findings.preferred_class1_route: Mirror the pinned FaceService separation: implement a modality-specific IrisService authenticate/cancel endpoint that requires USE_BIOMETRIC_INTERNAL, verifies the SystemUI Keyguard caller, and schedules through an iris sensor provider; expose it through a hidden IrisManager API and deliver explicit success/failure/error/lockout statuses into KeyguardUpdateMonitor. Keep IrisService generic IBiometricAuthenticator registration with BiometricService as separate registration/prompt plumbing, not as the Keyguard unlock callback. Keep public PromptInfo filtering unchanged and Convenience unavailable to apps.

class1_android16_cdd_requirements.presentation_attack_acceptance: Spoof and imposter acceptance no higher than 30% for Level A PAI species and 40% for Level B PAI species; CDD also sets a 40% maximum per PAI species.
class1_android16_cdd_requirements.attempt_policy: Rate limit biometric attempts; challenge primary credential after at most 20 false trials with at least 90 seconds backoff; disable biometrics once primary-authentication backoff has triggered.
class1_android16_cdd_requirements.credential_and_lifecycle: Require user confirmation of an existing or newly set device credential secured by TEE before adding biometrics; erase identifiable biometric data when user or primary credential is removed; honor KEYGUARD_DISABLE_IRIS.
class1_android16_cdd_requirements.fallback: Challenge primary credential at least every 24 hours, and after 4 hours idle or 3 failed biometric attempts.

findings.keyguard_vs_biometricprompt_boundary: The inspected AuthSession is for BiometricPrompt; StatusBarService.onBiometricAuthenticated does not establish the Keyguard modality callback path. Pinned Lineage KeyguardUpdateMonitor subscribes to FaceAuthenticationListener status events for face unlock; the installed SystemUI DEX contains FaceManager references. A system-only iris API and explicit callback/state integration are still missing.
findings.framework_transport_route: The phone has no iris VINTF HAL and the legacy IrisService is feature-gated, but a Camera2-backed SystemServer IrisService can use the existing camera provider without adding a biometric VINTF HAL. It still needs FEATURE_IRIS/product config, SystemServer startup, an iris modality service/client contract, SELinux permissions, provider scheduling, lifecycle and Keyguard-only caller checks. A separate Face AIDL route would mislabel iris and is not selected.

next_source_audit: establish stable repeatable illuminated sensor frames and validate an offline matcher before connecting authentication callbacks
implement a camera-backed IBiometricAuthenticator with real per-user enrollment/removal and lifecycle; the software Class 1 matcher should return no fabricated HAT

implement the camera-backed IrisService modality authenticate/cancel interface and provider scheduler following the pinned FaceService split (direct Keyguard modality request separate from prepareForAuthentication/BiometricPrompt); add a hidden IrisManager API and KeyguardUpdateMonitor iris status listener; retain generic registration separately, preserve public PromptInfo filtering, and do not add a new biometric VINTF HAL unless the chosen implementation actually introduces one
enable Class 1 only after FAR/SAR, credential-confirmed enrollment, DPM disable, lockout/backoff, user-switch and teardown gates are evidenced
keep the sensor out of Class 2/3 unless isolated matching, protected camera data/result paths and each class's acceptance-rate requirements are met

keyguard_evidence: KeyguardUpdateMonitor$21.<clinit> at DEX offset 0x4e6514 maps switch cases only for FINGERPRINT and FACE; it has no IRIS mapping.
KeyguardUpdateMonitor.isUnlockingWithBiometricAllowed(BiometricSourceType) at DEX offset 0x4e73fc returns false for an unmapped source type.
SystemUI DEX has FaceManager and FingerprintManager call paths and no IrisManager or TYPE_IRIS Keyguard request path. Generic BiometricSourceType callbacks exist but do not add an iris listener.

installed_systemui_readback.conclusion: The installed Keyguard cannot use an iris sensor for unlock as shipped. Adding only IrisService/IBiometricAuthenticator registration will not suffice.
